readme:
# RL Expert — Reinforcement Learning Skill Collection

A structured collection of Claude Code skills for designing, implementing, evaluating, and operating reinforcement learning systems. Skills are organized around five engineering roles that cover the full RL development lifecycle.

---

## Agent Skills (Orchestrators)

These top-level skills activate a specialized RL agent that coordinates the relevant atomic skills below.

| Skill | Trigger phrases |
|---|---|
| `rl-architect` | "activate the rl architect", "define the MDP", "formulate the RL problem", "design the reward function" |
| `rl-algo-engineer` | "activate the rl algo engineer", "implement the RL algorithm", "design neural networks", "implement PPO/SAC/DQN" |
| `rl-env-engineer` | "activate the rl env engineer", "implement the Gymnasium environment", "add domain randomization", "integrate MuJoCo" |
| `rl-evaluator` | "activate the rl evaluator", "evaluate the RL policy", "diagnose training failures", "analyze saliency maps" |
| `rl-mlops-engineer` | "activate the rl mlops engineer", "set up experiment tracking", "configure hyperparameter tuning", "scale distributed training" |

---

## Atomic Skills by Role

### RL Architect — Problem Formulation & Design

Skills for formalizing the RL problem before any code is written.

| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| `selecting-rl-strategy` | Compares algorithm families (PPO, SAC, DQN, TD3) against action space format, simulation cost, and stability requirements; produces a decision matrix |
| `defining-state-space` | Designs the observation space: sensor fusion, normalization strategy, and partial observability handling |
| `defining-action-space` | Formalizes discrete, continuous, multi-discrete, and hybrid action spaces |
| `defining-mdp-transition` | Specifies the Markov Decision Process: state transitions, episode termination, and discount factor |
| `designing-reward-function` | Designs dense/sparse reward signals, potential-based shaping, and multi-objective reward aggregation |
| `designing-hierarchical-rl` | Structures goal-conditioned and option-framework architectures for long-horizon tasks |
| `formulating-irl-and-imitation` | Formalizes inverse RL and imitation learning problem statements |
| `formulating-marl-architecture` | Designs multi-agent system topology: cooperative, competitive, and mixed settings |
| `blueprinting-system-architecture` | Produces the end-to-end system blueprint covering hardware placement, data flow, and distributed topology |

### RL Algorithm Engineer — Neural Networks & Training

Skills for implementing the learning algorithm and neural network components.

| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| `designing-policy-actor` | Implements actor networks with Gaussian/Categorical/Beta output distributions |
| `designing-value-critic` | Implements twin critic networks with Polyak averaging and Bellman targets |
| `designing-feature-extractor` | Builds CNN, ResNet, and multimodal feature extraction backbones |
| `implementing-loss-functions` | Implements PPO clip loss, SAC entropy objective, and TD3 policy gradient with gradient clipping |
| `configuring-replay-buffers` | Configures uniform, prioritized (PER), and HER replay buffers |
| `implementing-memory-models` | Adds LSTM/GRU recurrence and causal attention for partial observability |
| `implementing-offline-rl` | Implements CQL, IQL, and TD3+BC for offline dataset training |
| `implementing-imitation-learning` | Implements behavioral cloning and GAIL with discriminator networks |
| `implementing-marl-algorithms` | Implements QMIX, MADDPG, and CTDE training loops |
| `training-rlhf-reward-model` | Trains preference-based reward models using Bradley-Terry loss |

### RL Environment Engineer — Simulation & Environments

Skills for building and wrapping training environments.

| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| `implementing-gymnasium-env` | Scaffolds a spec-compliant Gymnasium environment with `reset`/`step`/`render` |
| `implementing-pettingzoo-marl-env` | Builds PettingZoo AEC and parallel multi-agent environments |
| `implementing-observation-wrappers` | Adds normalization (RunningMeanStd), frame stacking, and reward clipping wrappers |
| `implementing-temporal-wrappers` | Implements frame-skip and action-repeat wrappers |
| `implementing-domain-randomization` | Adds uniform and Automatic Domain Randomization (ADR) for sim-to-real transfer |
| `designing-adversarial-environments` | Builds PAIRED and adversarial curriculum environments |
| `integrating-physics-simulator` | Integrates MuJoCo, PyBullet, and Isaac Gym physics backends |
| `validating-env-compatibility` | Runs `gym.utils.env_checker` and SB3 compatibility checks across an environment suite |

### RL Evaluator — Testing & Analysis

Skills for assessing policy quality and diagnosing problems.

| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| `designing-deterministic-eval-loop` | Implements a seeded, deterministic evaluation harness with episode statistics |
| `diagnosing-training-failures` | Identifies gradient explosion, reward hacking, policy collapse, and other failure modes |
| `analyzing-saliency-and-values` | Produces saliency maps, value landscape plots, and attribution analysis |
| `creating-ood-robustness-tests` | Designs out-of-distribution test suites for environment perturbations |
| `conducting-adversarial-rl-testing` | Tests policy robustness against adversarial observation and action perturbations |
| `evaluating-marl-equilibria` | Measures Nash equilibria approximation and exploitability in multi-agent settings |
| `implementing-rendering-and-plotting` | Generates training curves, video rollouts, and diagnostic dashboards |

### RL MLOps Engineer — Infrastructure & Operations

Skills for experiment management, scaling, and deployment pipelines.

| Skill | What it does |
|---|---|
| `setting-up-experiment-tracking` | Configures Weights & Biases or MLflow with RL-specific metrics and run grouping |
| `configuring-hyperparameter-tuning` | Sets up Optuna or Ray Tune studies with RL-aware search spaces |
| `configuring-distributed-rollouts` | Scales data collection with Ray, sample-factory, or vectorized environment workers |
| `configuring-checkpoint-strategy` | Implements checkpoint scheduling, best-model selection, and resume logic |
| `setting-up-offline-rl-datasets` | Builds HDF5/D4RL-format offline datasets from rollout logs |
| `setting-up-rlhf-data-pipeline` | Constructs human preference collection and reward model training pipelines |

---

## Structure

Each skill lives in `skills/<skill-name>/` and follows a consistent layout:

```
skills/<skill-name>/
├── SKILL.md          # Skill definition and step-by-step instructions
├── scripts/          # Runnable Python scripts and utilities
└── references/       # Supporting theory, API references, and pattern guides
```

---

## Usage

Invoke any skill through Claude Code using the Skill tool or by using the natural language trigger phrases listed above. The five agent skills (`rl-architect`, `rl-algo-engineer`, etc.) serve as entry points that orchestrate the atomic skills appropriate for your task.
